label: conj:qbeta-ck-truncation-canonical
title: Canonical closed form for the $\mathfrak{Q}_\beta$ truncation coefficients $c_k$ ($k\geq 3$): only $c_2=-1$ is structural; $c_3=-2=J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(q{=}1)$ is a near-match; $c_{k\geq 3}$ are cal-anchored (open)
html:
The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta truncation coefficients differ in epistemic status. The tiering below records, for each rung, whether it is proved, near-matched, or calibration-anchored, so that its open status is explicit and checkable. A second axis, the Markov convention, cuts across all three tiers and is recorded separately at the end of this block: every numerical statement here is convention-C-frame, and the canonical convention is D.

The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta categorical precision ladder expresses the neutron \beta-decay Q-value substrate prediction as a convergent product of correction rungs around a Form-A baseline:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(q) \;=\; Q_{\text{base}}(q) \cdot \prod_{k\geq 2}\bigl(1 + c_k\,u^k\bigr),
  \qquad u \;=\; b\,\hbar_q^2 \;\approx\; 0.00852,

with b the Hoefsmit off-diagonal coupling on the seminormal V_{(2,1)} representation and \hbar_q = (q-1)/q. Because u \approx 0.00852, each rung adds roughly \log_{10}(1/u) \approx 2.07 decimal digits. The target precision fixes the truncation order N: N \geq \log_{10}(1/\varepsilon)/2.07 - 1; N is a precision setting rather than a criterion for whether a rung is canonical.

The status of the rung coefficients c_k is tiered:

  • c_2 = -1 — structural. The depth-2 coefficient is the exact u^2 coefficient of the explicit-factor product \prod_{k\ge2}(1 + c_k u^k), obtained by re-reading the Kashiwara \tilde f_1 geometric-tail factor (1 - b^2\,\hbar_q^4) in that form (prop:q-beta-categorical-precision-ladder). Being a constant, it is q_0-anchor-independent. Two scope limits: the factor (1 - b^2\hbar_q^4) is itself a definition, not a derived object, so "proved" overstates what is established; and "Taylor coefficient" is a statement about that series — the normalised series with the cosine factor inside has \tilde c_2 = c_2 - 1/8 = -9/8.
  • c_3 = -2 = J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(q{=}1) — near-match. The depth-3 coefficient matches the classical-limit Jones value of the two-component Hopf link, J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(q{=}1) = -2. This is a structural resemblance, not an exact identity. The empirical Taylor coefficient extracted at the substrate parameter is anchor-dependent. A true Taylor coefficient would be anchor-independent; c_3 is not.
  • c_k for k \geq 3 — cal-anchored (open). We obtain the higher coefficients by matching the truncated product to the measured Q-value. They are circular: they encode the calibration datum they attempt to predict, and shift with the substrate anchor. They are cached for downstream reuse but carry no predictive content.

Convention frame (cuts across every tier above). The tiers record epistemic status. They do not record which Markov convention the numbers were computed in, and that is the larger caveat of the two. Every value in this block — c_2 = -1, c_3 = -2, and the cal-anchored c_{k\ge3} — was obtained with the Markov parameter z_C = \sqrt{q}/(q+1) (convention C), which is excised; the canonical Markov parameter is z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) (convention D).

The convention enters at exactly one place: the N{=}1 eigenphase \alpha = (z-1)\,h/2, where h = q - q^{-1}. The four tail factors — the rungs k = 2,\ldots,5 of the product above — are built from b and \hbar_q alone and never mention z. But every extracted c_k is obtained by dividing the measured Q-value through a partial product that begins with the N{=}1 factor, so that single entry point propagates into all of them. Measured at 60 decimal places, re-extracting under convention D:

convention C convention D
implied c_2 -1.017623798 -9.298862871
c_3 (proton anchor) -2.069342577115168 -974.4318877467484
distance to -\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 0 972.402004534

For scale, the caveat the c_3 tier above does carry — anchor dependence — is worth 0.0495 across the two pins. The convention shift is worth 972.36, roughly twenty thousand times larger. Both are real; only one was recorded.

One pillar is convention-immune and does not need re-establishing: the cross-anchor swing, whose ratio between the two conventions is 1.00522 because its dominant source — the sensitivity of the Form-A baseline Q_{\text{base}}(q) divided by u^3 — is z-free. So the verdict that c_3 is refuted as a real-q fibre element survives the convention change. It is the value-level near-matches that do not.

Re-deriving the ladder under D is not a substitution of z_D into the existing expressions — that is proved invalid (QOU.QBeta.decayLadder_zC_threeRow_ne_zero). It requires deriving the D-frame eigenphase first, after which the ansatz above is reusable as it stands and the five values are re-extracted from it.

Conjecture (open). For every k \geq 3 there exists a canonical, substrate-only, q_0-anchor-independent closed form for the truncation coefficient c_k — a genuine Taylor coefficient of a single underlying q-series (a Habiro element) rather than a calibration-anchored near-match.

The expected mechanism mirrors the \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} next-order factor resolution: identify the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta Habiro element, the q-series whose Taylor coefficients are the c_k. Such an element would make each c_{k\geq 3} exact and anchor-independent, convert the per-rung magnitude |c_{N+1}\,u^{N+1}| into a rigorous arbitrary-order truncation bound, and elevate the precision-order formula N(\varepsilon) from heuristic to derivation. Until then, higher rungs serve as a calibration record, not a prediction.
heading: Conjecture
